title: Autosweep tuner for attention kernel sensitivity (v3 layout) and safe fallback shims
creator: Carlos Mendes
description: Objective: Implement an automated 'autosweep' tuner that probes attention kernel configurations (tile sizes, micro-tiling, workspace layouts, quant-mode toggles) and detects model/hardware combinations sensitive to the FlashAttention v3 memory layout. When sensitivity or throughput regressions are detected, the system should surface a safe compatibility shim and automatically route affected requests to a validated fallback kernel without impacting correctness or violating latency SLOs.
background: Recent customer canaries exposed intermittent 10-30% tail-latency regressions for certain sequence-length distributions on Ampere/Hopper GPUs after enabling FlashAttention v3 layout optimizations. Existing kernel selection heuristics use static matrix-profile thresholds and don't capture runtime layout interactions (leading-dimension strides, alignment padding, per-layer quantization state). Manual mitigation (force-v2 layout) reduces throughput for other workloads. We need a low-risk, data-driven way to discover and mitigate these regressions per model/profile.
technical_approach: 1) Lightweight online profiler: implement a non-blocking probe that runs small representative microbenchmarks for a new kernel variant on a subset of warm requests (probe ratio configurable). 2) Autosweep strategy: sweep a compact parameter space (tile dims, ephemeral quant flag, layout-stride transform) rather than exhaustive combinations — use Bayesian/greedy search prioritizing parameters historically correlated with regressions. 3) Compatibility shim: when a layout-sensitive regression is found, apply a minimal transform (e.g., stride-preserve tensor transpose or per-layer PAD correction) to restore v2-compatibility for affected layers and mark kernel variant as 'shimmed' in routing metadata. 4) Safe fallback queue: create a short-circuit routing policy to send affected model/route to an already validated v2-style kernel variant while monitoring error and latency deltas. 5) Telemetry gates: only flip routing after meeting statistical significance thresholds and no correctness failures. 6) Rollout: start in canary (10% traffic) with auto-rollback if regression persists, then widen. 7) Backward compatibility: ensure probes are idempotent and can be disabled via runtime config.
acceptance_criteria: Autosweep probe runs without adding >1ms median latency to unaffected requests when probe_ratio=0.01
System detects a layout-induced regression in synthetic and real traces and recommends a shim or fallback within 30 minutes of observing pattern
Fallback routing reduces tail latency by >=15% for affected traces versus pre-mitigation baseline without increasing error rate
No correctness regressions introduced by shim transformations (parity tests pass across representative prompt set)
Feature rollout includes canary with automatic rollback and telemetry visible in Console dashboard
